documents.title: Specification and design-document system
documents.purpose: Authors write Markdown and metadata; the tool checks them and generates navigation and agent reading packages.
documents.audience: Specification and design-document authors, reviewers and tool implementers familiar with Markdown links, headings and basic Git snapshots.
documents.scope: Single-file and multi-file specifications and designs: who owns meanings and values, how checking and review work, and how agents receive material captured from one repository version.
documents.non_goals: Product contracts, HTML publication, a renderer, expression evaluation, semantic measurement conversion, independent requirement stores and general prose formatting.

sections.summary: Choose a reading path and see which authored sources produce checked navigation and agent input.
Follow a wrong capacity link through a visible error, correction, regenerated map and complete review input.
Place meanings and values once, then connect reading order, accepted names and direct links to those homes.
Connect obligations, refusals and evidence, then determine which tests a changed contract brings into review.
Run the pinned checker, distinguish errors from warnings and rebuild valid navigation after a failed or interrupted generation.
Select complete explanations from one snapshot and refuse unknown, stale or excessive assignments before dispatch.
Assign source ownership, review technical meaning and qualify real authoring without mistaking a structural pass for reader acceptance.
Find the observable obligations for authoring, checking, generation, context and review with reciprocal verification links.
Distinguish settled source and tool choices from unresolved differences between rules, code and approved intent.
Look up exact metadata keys, declaration grammar and callable assignments after learning what each source contributes.
Reproduce the bounded-batch fixture in an independent repository and inspect the exact files used throughout the tour.
Choose the command or diagnostic remedy for the batch correction and inspect executable-selector audit results.
Find behavioral regressions and real-run evidence that prove each obligation, including reader understanding and visible recovery.

documents.title: Rule changes
documents.purpose: Report rule text changes and require an explicit review disposition for each item.
documents.audience: Maintainers and review-service integrators familiar with Git revisions and review packs.
documents.scope: Protected Markdown comparison, review context and mandatory audit dispatch.
documents.non_goals: Automatic semantic approval, sentence-lock test deletion and service implementation.

sections.summary: Read the purpose and review boundary.
Follow a removal, weakening, move and re-wrap.
Compare protected text and preserve complete evidence.
Find the required report and review results.
Read the operator decision and the settled lead decisions.
Identify the remaining service integration.
Configure coverage and call the shared selector.
Run behavior checks and inspect reviewer obligations.

documents.title: Repository checks
documents.purpose: Repository checks run a repository's deterministic rule checks before each commit, before each push and in CI, from one declared configuration.
documents.audience: House Rules maintainers and repository owners familiar with Git hooks and CI workflows.
documents.scope: The check configuration, the check runner, built-in checks, the install procedure, agent session status and the rule line.
documents.non_goals: Judgment rules that need a reviewer, prose warnings, Warden changes and implementation in this change.

sections.summary: Read what repository checks do and who runs them.
See what exists today, what was measured and the constraints.
Follow one install, a refused commit and its fix.
Name the House Rules layer and declare checks in one file, and write a check to the command contract.
See when each check runs, what it reads and how pre-commit stays fast.
Install hooks and CI without breaking other tools, and connect agent sessions.
Know which House Rules commit a run resolves its layer to, what it logs and what works without a network.
Review overrides, and know which rules stay with reviewers.
Apply the configuration to another naming style and to a repository without specifications.
Find the obligations each mechanism must meet.
Read each choice, its authority and the alternatives it rejects.
Confirm that no design choice remains open.
Plan the implementation pull requests and adoption.
Look up configuration fields, built-ins, commands and the report format.
See the planned demonstrations for each requirement.

documents.title: Layered House Rules configuration
documents.purpose: Layered House Rules configuration lets every repository say which House Rules version and which further rule and setting repositories it uses, and makes every tool resolve them from the repository it runs in.
documents.audience: House Rules maintainers, repository owners and teams adopting House Rules, familiar with Git branches and commits, JSON and the repository checks design.
documents.scope: The repository, layer and global configuration files, version resolution and its cache, the house-rules command, link mode, Git isolation for checks, and how every consumer resolves.
documents.non_goals: New language checks, a runner other than House Rules', a package registry, and implementation in this change.

sections.summary: Read what layered configuration does and which tools resolve it.
See how House Rules reaches tools today and the constraints the design meets.
Follow a Rust repository with two custom layers from its file to a refused commit and a session.
Declare layers, profiles and settings, and predict the effective value of every key.
Know how a ref becomes a commit, where its files live, and what works offline or linked.
Find where each tool reads the configuration and how checks avoid personal Git settings.
Apply the design to a default repository, no configuration, link mode, a Warden review and an offline run.
Find the obligations each mechanism must meet.
Read the operator's decisions with their words, the lead's recommendations and the design choices.
See which questions stay open after the approval.
Move a machine from one checkout to the command, and adopt the file in a repository.
Plan the implementation pull requests and their order.
Look up schemas, commands, variables, record formats, messages and naming conventions.
See the planned demonstrations for each requirement.
